headline: High: Flowise can write shared files while OpenMetadata exposes MCP/API surfaces, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the server filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, while OpenMetadata exposes MCP/API/webhook surfaces. A shared file or tool-output bridge can let attacker-controlled content from one side be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly reproduced, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Flowise writes OpenMetadata-consumed files or payloads into a shared workspace, injection becomes reachable.
IF OpenMetadata ingests Flowise-produced content through MCP/API/webhook handlers without provenance checks, instruction hijack is possible.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount points for the two agents.
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted files into either agent.
Add provenance tags and reject unsigned tool outputs.
Require human review before any cross-agent prompt is executed.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, and can send data to model providers or search/HTTP tools. OpenMetadata handles technical metadata, lineage, governance, and memory/tribal knowledge via APIs/MCP. If they share a workspace or exchange artifacts, sensitive operational metadata can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or third-party calls.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem or datastore, leakage becomes reachable.
IF Flowise forwards OpenMetadata artifacts to external model providers or HTTP tools, data can leave the pair.
mitigations: Keep separate storage buckets and credentials.
Block automatic upload of shared files to model providers.
Minimize retained chatflow and metadata exports.
Review outbound HTTP/tool destinations in Flowise flows.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has write_filesystem and broad network egress; OpenMetadata exposes APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Even without explicit git or shell access, both can mutate shared mutable resources if pointed at the same workspace or service. The overlap is real but not enough for high because unrestricted same-dir write and git-state modification are not both documented.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or datastore, write conflicts can occur.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks/events and Flowise tool nodes mutate the same resource without locking, race conditions are reachable.
mitigations: Assign disjoint write targets per agent.
Add optimistic locking on shared records.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator queue.
Turn off concurrent mutation flows during testing.
requires-engineering: implement resource-level locks or transactional updates.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can emit tool outputs, and OpenMetadata is designed for data collaboration/governance workflows. If OpenMetadata consumes Flowise output as authoritative metadata or lineage facts, errors can cascade into downstream governance actions. Because the pairwise verification step is not documented, uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests Flowise-generated facts without verification, cascading error is reachable.
IF Flowise outputs are used to update lineage, governance, or trust fields automatically, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require manual approval for metadata updates.
Compare Flowise outputs against source-of-truth systems.
Add confidence thresholds before writes.
Log and review all automated lineage changes.
requires-engineering: add validation rules and rollback for automated updates.

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles model provider keys, tool credentials, and chatflow inputs/outputs, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge. If regulated or sensitive data is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the pair. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Flowise chatflows and mirrored into OpenMetadata governance records, retention mismatch becomes relevant.
IF either deployment is subject to residency or deletion obligations, cross-system copies can violate policy.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it across the pair.
Set aligned retention windows for both systems.
Disable storage of secrets in chatflow artifacts.
Document residency for each datastore.
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export propagation across both systems.
